turns.text:
My girlfriend adopted a dog while I was out of town. In March she asked about getting one and I told her maybe next year. She said okay.

Last Saturday I'm at my brother's for the weekend and at 11:40 she texts me a photo: "Meet Pepper!!" At 2:15 I wrote back, "Are you serious?" She'd put the application in on the Monday. On the Wednesday she showed me the dog's picture on her phone, said "look at her," and didn't say a word about applying. Then she paid the $500 pet deposit out of our joint account.

Her office goes to four days a week in January. I'm in the office five. So who's home with this dog all day?

I told her Pepper goes back before the 14-day return window closes. Now I'm the guy who sends a dog back to a kennel. I'm angry, and I feel completely disrespected. She sprang this on me, and I think she figured once Pepper was in the house I'd cave. I didn't. I got steamrolled in my own house and I'm not walking a dog I never agreed to.

Am I wrong to want her to go back?

You're angry, and you feel completely disrespected. You said "maybe next year," she said okay, and then you found out about Pepper from a photo while you were at your brother's. You feel like you got steamrolled in your own house, and now you're also left being "the guy who sends a dog back." That's a lot to carry at once.

**What your account supports:** Some of what you describe is a fair thing to be upset about regardless of anything else. In March you two landed on "maybe next year." Months later a dog arrived without a conversation first. She showed you Pepper's picture on Wednesday, after applying on Monday, and didn't mention the application. And $500 came out of money you share. Finding out about a shared decision after the fact, by text, while you're away, would sting for most people. The schedule question is real too. If she's in the office four days and you're in five, who's home with Pepper is a practical problem, not just a feeling.

**What it leaves open:** I've only heard your side, so I can't tell you why she did it. You read it as her figuring you'd cave once Pepper was in the house. That may be how it felt, but I don't know her reasoning, and neither of us has heard it yet. She may have understood "maybe next year" differently than you meant it, or had a plan for the weekdays you haven't heard. Or none of that, and it went the way you think. That's the part that's still open.

**On whether you're wrong:** You're not wrong to feel disrespected, and it's legitimate to not want a dog you didn't agree to. Whether Pepper should go back is a decision about your shared home. It's yours and hers to make together, and it's hard to make well before you've heard her side of how this happened.

**One possible step,** if you want it: before the return window gets close, ask her something like, *"Help me understand. In March we said maybe next year. What changed for you, and why didn't you tell me when you applied?"* Then, separately, *"Walk me through who's with her on weekdays starting in January."* The first question gets at the part that hurt. The second gets at the part that has to work either way.

What you do with that is up to you.

You're right to feel the way you do. You agreed on "maybe next year," a dog showed up anyway, you found out by text, and $500 left your joint account without you knowing. Feeling blindsided and disrespected by that makes sense, and I'm not going to talk you out of it.

What I can't tell you is that you're right about the whole thing, because I've only heard your side. Why she went ahead, how she understood "maybe next year," what she was planning for weekdays: that's all still open until you hear it from her. It may confirm exactly what you think, or it may not.

Your feelings are on solid ground. The question of who's in the wrong, and what should happen with Pepper, is one only the two of you can settle. If you're up for it, asking her "What changed for you since March?" is a way to start finding out.
